title: Now Let Us Come Before Him
description: Now Let Us Come Before Him in Tonic Solfa to ST. BEES, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 14 verses and a piano.
about: Paul Gerhardt wrote these words in German. John Kelly's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 174.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BEES; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now let us come be-fore Him, With songs and prayers a-dore Him, Who to our life from hea-ven All need-ed strength hath giv-en.

lines: Now let us come before Him,
With songs and prayers adore Him,
Who to our life from heaven
The stream of years is flowing,
And pass through times of anguish,
When need and woe distress them,
In vain is all our doing;
Our thanks to Thee we render,
O God of mercy, hear us;
Our Father, be Thou near us;
Be Thou our Fount of gladness.
To all that bow before Thee
And for Thy grace implore Thee,
In all our ways, Lord, own us;
To all, e’en to the lowest.
And of the poor and needy
That He may make us glorious
Thou Life, whence our life floweth;
Grant, Lord, these New Year’s favors.

licence: Public domain: Paul Gerhardt died in 1676; John Kelly died in 1890.
credits: Words by Paul Gerhardt (1607–1676), translated by John Kelly (1833–1890), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. BEES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
